entries.final_answer: The operator dispatches docs-pages.yml from main with canary=true in an announced window with docs merges frozen. The run builds the doc-kitty site through the shared docs-site-build.yml (D-11), deploys it to Pages, probes a ledger-derived sample of D-13 URL classes on https://docs.spec-kitty.ai, then always rebuilds and redeploys DocFX and fails the run if the probe failed. Answered from the operator brief for #6938 PR A.
entries.question: Who starts the canary, when, and what must it prove?

entries.final_answer: Derived from the committed ledgers (url-baseline.txt, moves.yaml, legacy-redirects.json), never a hand list: one .html key to its own page, one moved-chain key, one live dir/index.html (rule 3), one dir/README.html, one directory URL, plus the site root, /llms.txt and one retired /kitty-specs/ route expected 404. Stubs must name the map's target and the target must serve 200. Answered from the operator brief.
entries.question: Which URL classes does the probe check, and how is the sample chosen?

entries.final_answer: The non-canary push and dispatch path stays DocFX behaviour; deploy stays main-only and core-repository-only; the Pages probe-then-configure job stays; the canary never leaves the doc-kitty site live (DocFX always redeployed); the cutover is a later PR B and not done here. Answered from the operator brief.
entries.question: What must always hold?

entries.final_answer: The DocFX build job is untouched and builds in parallel; the canary publishes only after both the shared doc-kitty build and the DocFX build succeeded; the probe runs after the canary publish; the existing deploy job waits on the probe and runs on !cancelled() || canary, so it republishes DocFX whatever the probe said, while its default-path semantics are equivalent. Brief-derived engineering decision.
